headline: Karissa had a fall at home on 2026-09-23 and an ED visit for dehydration and dizziness on 2026-11-05. She is now at high fall risk, and PT recommendations are in place.

items.statement: Karissa fell in the bathroom at night at home on 2026-09-23. Her son Marcus found her on the floor. She denied head strike and loss of consciousness, and no injury was found. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: All details (date, bathroom at night, son Marcus found her, denied head strike/LOC, no injury, high fall risk, PT referral) match the nursing note.

items.statement: She was seen in the partner hospital ED on 2026-11-05 for dehydration and dizziness. She was treated and released the same day with no new medications. PCP follow-up on 2026-11-11 found her back to baseline per her son, discharge medications were reviewed, and the PCP planned close monitoring over the next two weeks.
items.verifier_note: ED visit 11/5 for dehydration and dizziness, treated and released, no new meds, and PCP 11/11 follow-up with baseline per son, discharge meds reviewed, close monitoring over two weeks are all in the notes and encounter record.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-01 found a slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars. PT will see her twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: PT note matches: slow unsteady gait, intermittent cane, TUG 19 s, front-wheeled walker, home safety eval, grab bars, twice weekly strength and balance.

items.statement: The notes in this period do not show whether the walker, home safety evaluation, or grab bars have been put in place. They also do not show the results of the PCP's two-week monitoring after the 2026-11-11 visit.
items.verifier_note: The cited notes contain no information on implementation of the walker, home safety evaluation, or grab bars, nor on results of the two-week monitoring. The absence statement is accurate for these sources.
